utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. We will be sitting for the whole of this week pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Judge Morrison should be away due to his obligation in his country. Good morning, witness, I hope you had a good weekend.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Excellencies, good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please help us understand what happened exactly and in which way. Did I understand things correctly? Were you hiding for all of two months? Is that right? And if so, where?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I was hiding for about two months from 10 July until 20 September, or rather to be more precise, 10 September. I hid on the outskirts of the village, in the corn fields and near the woods close to the village. From time to time I did go home. But I didn't go to my own home actually. I went to the house of a relative of mine that was nearby, that was near the woods and the corn field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who was there at the house of that relative?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That relative had sons but he himself, at the time, was 65, or rather, 70 years old. He had two daughters and his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why were you hiding?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, in our village, all men from age 18 to 65 were taken in, and I saw that some of them had been killed too. I didn't know about the rest. And then that evening, after the 10th, when I returned home, they told me, since actually on the same day, on two or three times, the army passed through the village and searched the houses to see whether anyone was left, and they were looking for weapons and whatever else, of course I didn't dare stay at home. I had to stay outside my house, otherwise they would have taken me away probably, had they found me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-hah. And then you got in touch with your neighbour, not to mention his name, and he helped you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was my sister that established contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you came to Kljuc and how much time did you spend in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven or eight days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it hard to get on to that list for transport to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't really know about that. But I know that certain documentation had to be taken care of first. For instance, one had to have a proper ID, then also proper land documents, tax documents, and, of course, at the police station, you get some kind of document allowing you to leave, and then with that you buy a ticket.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-hah. And then you pay the ticket - don't you? - the entire convoy does.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes, a certain person had to pay a certain amount of money.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it a long list or did a person have to wait for a long time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometimes you'd have to wait for seven, eight or 10 days. Since it wasn't just one convoy, there were several convoys going from Kljuc, to tell you the truth, I didn't really go for that ticket so I don't really know that well how that went but I know that my folks had to wait three or four days until they managed to get tickets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it that way for all or was it only for your family?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For all, for all citizens of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under whose control was Kljuc then?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, it was basically the police of the then-Republika Srpska. I mean at that time. So it was only natural that all power was in the hands of ethnic Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm a bit confused now. How come that Serbs, Serb authorities, just let you be, whereas you were the survivor of such a drastic incident and this neighbour of yours disregards that, and the authorities disregard that, they just don't care and they let you go. Do you have any explanation how come that happened?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said, I didn't go to buy the tickets. Because some friends of mine bought two tickets. Due to health problems, they could not leave so my sister took these two tickets from them. When they were sending convoys, trucks, buses, I personally got on to a trailer truck and they didn't ask me who I was and what I was doing. It was just important to have that coupon, that ticket, and to board the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But this neighbour did know that you had survived that and he let you go, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had he known, he probably wouldn't have taken me away at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he did not know that you were on that bus?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't know at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the authorities in Kljuc? Did they know that you were a survivor of that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you reported to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: After a while, after a bit of rest, as you describe in your statements, you joined one particular unit. What was that unit? You don't have to say it, never mind, never mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We will redact line 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you get a certificate as to your participation in the war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So from which date does your participation in the war run?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't wish to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we move into closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's see how these people are listed on lists of sehids, combatants, can you tell us what the word "sehid" means, exactly?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be honest with you, and I think I mentioned this recently, in order for their families to actually get some compensation, to get some kind of compensation, and have some means of subsistence, they would then name their relatives who had been killed as sehids in order for them to qualify for certain -- to qualify for certain compensation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that would be fraud, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we now please see D115, page 3 -- yes, that's what he said in translation. In relation to the fraud that I asked about, the witness said yes, something to that effect. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. What I -- as I said already, in order for them to qualify for certain compensation because these families had to live off of something, there were all these children whose fathers had been killed, they had to go to school and so on, so they did have to qualify for certain rights so that they would get compensation to have some means of subsistence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe we did have the correct text before, 1D1115, page 33, but my question was: Is this how they defrauded the state?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: D1115, D. That is an exhibit already, D1115. About this fraud, how many men were listed as sehids, whereas they weren't sehids, and what was the scope of this fraud that was perpetrated there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you waited for these seven months to tell this story. Why didn't you talk about this as soon as you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I came back, when I arrived, when I actually reached the free territory, I did not even leave my -- the premises where I was staying for two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we now please see page 333? Let me just see if this is the correct document? In e-court, that's page 333. Can you see Domazet, Fuad Domazet's name on this list? And you can also see the name of Smajo Cajic.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There are a lot of people from Kljuc. Were all these people civilians who are now listed as sehids?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only the people from Biljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at this page? Do you see how many people there are listed as being from Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they all just put down Kljuc but most of these people were from Biljani. Dedic, the Dedic people, are from another town. But as I've already said, in order to qualify for certain compensation, this is what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, can you see the name of Cajic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I did. I see Avdo and Smajo Cajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you also see the Cehics and then the Domazets, all these people were from Kljuc and not a single one of them was a fighter, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, in Biljani, out of those 200 or so people in Biljani, not a single bullet was shot. All the weapons had been surrendered, they were all taken to this school, they all went to the school, reported there to the elementary school in Biljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you did not really answer my question, my original question. What is the meaning of the word "sehids"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sehid is a person who gets killed on God's path, I'll be quite frank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's an Islamic holy warrior, correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't put it that way. When you're defending your hearth, you would also be a sehid or when you get killed on God's path that would also be a sehid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now let's go back to the incident itself. You got on the bus. How many people were on the bus?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 70 men approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Did we need to stay in private session for the whole of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [In English] No, no. I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you're suggesting going back to open session now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that number of people got on the bus and there was not a single soldier or officer on that bus?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were only the driver, who was in the front, and two or three soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But in your statements, you said that there wasn't a single soldier.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're probably right. It was the military police who were on the bus then, if we want to be very precise. But I said that when the bus set off, two more policemen got on the bus, they were looking for some four men or so, and then we started off and then they got on the bus again, they asked us all to get on another bus, and that's how it went.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But when you set off, there was not a single soldier or officer, correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I may have -- I don't know. Maybe I didn't mention that because no one had asked about it but I didn't really see much. I was seated in the back of the bus, next to the back door, rear door, and that's where I spent most of the time, on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how long then did the bus go before you were stopped?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we just covered some 100 metres or so and then it stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Outside whose house did you stop?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some 20 to 30 metres beyond Alic, Mehmed, across from Habir's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then they asked for two or four men to get off the bus, strong men.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that the first time the bus stopped was some ten metres later, and they asked for four strong men to get off the bus, and then I raised my head and I recognised (redacted) I recalled also this other person, Mujo from Krnojevic [phoen] and there were two other men, I saw them and they got off the bus, out the front door. I thought they needed them to do some work, to perform some labour or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see. And then you road for another 100 metres or so?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. After a few moments, the bus set off again and the driver already then said that they couldn't really reach Kljuc because the bus was overcrowded. So then he drove on for some 100 metres more and then we stopped again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then they said that some of you should move to another bus, correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And then someone said, "Will you open the back door and left the first five, the five people who are closest to the door get off?" And when they did, I was among those five who got off the bus. There were also Fikret Balagic, Avdic, Alija, Besim Avdic and Rufad. They I don't know his last name. They took us past the bus and some ten metres behind there was another bus but they didn't take us to that bus. First, they let us get on the bus through the back door. However, when we did that, they -- when we headed for the back door they actually took us behind the house of Mehmed and they just took us behind the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see now page 329, please? That's D1115, the document we had a few moments ago on the screen. Would you please take a look at the lower third of the page, the bottom third of the list, the names that you mentioned, the Balagics for instance?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fikret Balagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the man you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: His name appears under the name Sulejman Bajric?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me just take a look, Elmir, no, that's not him, no. Fikret was an older man. He used to work in the municipality as the deputy chairman or something, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was his father's name?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was Arif.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can you see under number 32780 --

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see it now. Yes, that could be the man because he was born in 1940.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you find the other names? All those names that you mentioned, they are all on listed here as sehids. Can you please find them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's true they are listed as sehids.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you please explain this? After some hundred metres or so, you were stopped and then you were taken towards a house.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were taken outside the house, in front of that house, and then at one point they stopped, they said, we have to stop, they needed to get something or something, but because the barrel was already in my mouth, they pushed me with the gun forward, and I saw at that time a relative of mine who was already on the ground, and we just stepped over them. I think Rufad then tried to flee. He ran towards the right. These men followed him. I ran to the left, Besim after me and I just heard them calling after us, "stop, fuck your balija mothers" and then they started shooting. This would have been some ten metres away or so where they were shooting from. First I only saw Besim, as I stepped in front of him I saw Besim falling down and then I also dropped to the ground, I don't know why. Anyway, when he dropped to the ground, I did too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, what I am not clear on is this: What about those people who had been taken off a hundred metres earlier and allegedly had been shot? How was it that now you could see them in front of you, a hundred metres away, further off?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was just telling you now. They asked for those four men to be taken off the bus. And I was taken off the bus with four other men, some 100 metres later. They had probably been taken outside the same house or behind the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But how was it that they could be in front of you when you rode on the bus?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, when we stopped, when these four men were taken off the bus, the four strong men, the driver lingered there for a while and then he said that we couldn't reach Kljuc we were so overcrowded and then he started moving and some ten metres later he stopped again and sort of wondered how we could go on and then -- so this could have been some five minutes or so and then he moved 100 metres further.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I understand but they were taken a hundred metres away, whereas you stopped, your bus stopped so how come the bus -- you were not faster than them? How did they happen to be in your way?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you they were taken away five minutes earlier. I walked some ten metres only. If you give me a map I can show you. I did not have time to count metres or minutes. Those minutes lasted forever, to all of us who were waiting in all that uncertainty, not knowing what's going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when you fell to the ground, was it next to Besim?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, next to Besim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your first statement you said you fell over his body.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's possible but I was so close to Besim, I could have touched him if I stretched my arm. I don't really remember every detail of it any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So those 65 continued peacefully on their way to Kljuc, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some five, six minutes later, as I think I said in my statement, that's how long it lasted and then two or three minutes later, they said, "Come back quickly. We are going on to Kljuc." And according to some statements of eyewitnesses on the road to Velagici, there were two buses, and it's true there were two buses, but I know that in the second bus, as we were passing by, there were no civilians. I just saw a couple of soldiers. I think I said that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, those people who were put on the same bus with you continued some five minutes later. Will you give us some names of these people who can confirm your story?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I give you their names? They were all killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that the others stayed 90 minutes and then today you say later it was a couple of minutes. Today you are saying five minutes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said. I said the whole killing, the whole process, lasted seven to nine hours. I cannot tell you exactly how long it was. I didn't have a watch and I didn't mind the time, and that time from the point when we left the school until the end, it was some hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But in this incident, you were stopped 100 metres after you started, just give me a few names of people or the name of the unit. Who stopped you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you before, the driver said he couldn't get to Kljuc because we were too many on the bus, and we were stopped. Now, who stopped us, who ordered this transfer, I don't know. You are better placed to know than I. Maybe you have some lists. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So after the killing of those four men, did anyone remain alive out of the other five people who got off the bus?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you survived and all of it took no more than five minutes but in your later statements you said they stayed there for another hour, hour and a half, they were drunken, they were singing and you could infer to those men had been killed and then those soldiers left. Do you know where?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Karadzic is confusing two incidents. I think the witness is trying to explain that but the hour and a half is after when the witness had been lying still on the ground. I think the witness is trying to answer that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, please proceed to answer the question, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's correct. And that's what I said. It was no more than five minutes between the time when we were taken off the bus to the point when the bus continued to Kljuc. I remained on the same spot for an hour, perhaps more, perhaps an hour and a half. In that time, within five minutes, soldiers came. Of course, I didn't see them but I could hear them well. They first came to that house and one of them even went around the house calling, "Come on, there are some more dead men here." And somebody said, "I've had enough. I'm fed up." And those soldiers stayed around for another hour after the bus left. Some were saying, "Let's burn this down." Others said, "Let's not do that. Maybe somebody can use it." And then they brought drinks and they were talking and drinking before they left. In both directions. And I remained for another ten, 15 minutes after things got quiet. Or perhaps it was an hour. I don't know. I didn't have a watch. I didn't know how long it was. But after things got quiet, when I thought that the soldiers had gone, I ran away to the woods nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you said in one statement, witness, that you were lying for ten, 15 minutes before you got up.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know how it is. I say something and then the interpreter doesn't interpret it correctly. It couldn't have been that long. I lay on the ground five minutes before the soldiers left. But after they left, I stayed for another half an hour, not less, before I got up and ran.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, do you have more to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, your Excellency. There is a lot of ground to cover. Many inconsistencies, many discrepancies and to establish the truth we need to know what happened and whether it happened exactly as he describes it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Your time was up about ten minutes ago. But just -- we will consult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please conclude in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that towards the end of June, when soldiers came from Palanka and rounded up people according to a list, one of the soldiers wanted to kill them and the commander said, the houses had been searched, they were innocent and had to be released, correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said the soldier was reluctant to kill them and then the commander asked, "What are we going to do with these three, four men? Take them behind the house." The soldier said, "I can't do it." And the commander said, "Then take them home." And they took the bus to the next hamlet. That's what I said and that's what my statement says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll find it now to see exactly what you said.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are looking for it, do you deny, witness, that there were three companies in Biljani?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, what kind of companies?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Three companies of the Muslim army, commanded by Amir Avdic and Ale Mujezinovic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I honestly know nothing about it and I'm telling you that in Biljani in the course of 1992, not a single bullet was fired. And whatever hunting weapons there had been were surrendered, you can find it in statements, you can find it in reports, and you can find it in police reports, that there was not a single bullet fired in Biljani in 1992 while the Muslims were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that Smail Domazet was the commander of a platoon?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about Zijad Abdic in Brkici?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there. I don't know about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about your relative -- sorry. Maybe it can be redacted but I didn't say the last name. When the search was conducted in Brkici, you said no weapons were found and then one soldier wanted to take revenge and the officer stopped him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that, in Biljani, outside our houses, my brother told me about this when he returned. One soldier was sharpening a knife and was saying, "I'm going to slit the throat of the dark-haired one." But they didn't do anything. They went to the next hamlet and from Atkovci [phoen] they were returned to Domazet and in Domazeti with the consent of one Serb, who testified that those men were good people and good neighbours, those men were returned to their homes. Mladjo and Boro took them away that morning, spent the entire day with them, and the same evening returned them home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They returned them -- they took them back in their own cars?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not dare to go back alone because of the army so they were looking for somebody to escort them to Brkici and Domazeti, so Boro and Mladjo walked with them to Brkici village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statement of 3 June 2000, paragraph 2, you stated around 50 men were brought to the schoolhouse in Kljuc to be interrogated. After that, ten were released while the remaining 40 were sent to Manjaca. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true because out of those ten, I know two or three who returned in June 1992, they came to Biljani, and they told us that the others had remained in Kljuc, in the schoolhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say here you did not believe that the Green Berets were attacking although the policemen told you they were, and you were in fact put in the schoolhouse for your own safety?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said, "How can there be talk about any Green Berets?" He was just standing there in the doorway. He said, "We will deal with them quickly."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you didn't believe him. You thought there were no Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there were no Green Berets. Not a single bullet was fired in Biljani. And in around the place, there was not a single incident. How could the Green Berets suddenly appear out of nowhere at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say several times that some people went somewhere and then volleys of automatic fire were heard.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As they were taking people out of the school, as they took someone out of the school, two or three minutes later you would hear automatic fire. For instance, Omer Dervisevic was taken out first, and then Ale Cajic and as they were getting out, you could hear automatic fire within two or three minutes or within ten minutes. I didn't -- I wasn't watching the time. Every time someone was taken out, you could hear very soon the sound of automatic fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you didn't see what happened to those people?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Looking out of the classroom you could only see the soldiers under the trees and you could see those standing on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you stated, on 3 June, page 345, that you heard somebody saying, "It should never have happened. They should have been taken to Kljuc, the killing should not have happened. We were supposed to be taken to Kljuc"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember all of my statements. I gave a number of statements, in some I stated one thing that I omitted in another. I don't know about this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you hear the man saying that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I understood it differently. As I was sitting on the bus, in the back of the bus, and when the bus was already filled up, somebody said, "What are we going to do with the rest who are still inside the school?" Somebody else answered, "Just kill them all. We don't need them."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the incident where you were the victim. After that, soldiers came, you say, they started talking, somebody said, "This shouldn't have happened."

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. That was after the execution. As I was lying on the ground behind the house, with the others, there was -- they were saying all sorts of things and I told you it was at least half an hour that they were talking. One of them even stopped his friend from burning down the house while the others were shouting, "Torch it all." Somebody said, "No, we shouldn't." They were all expressing their different opinions. That's normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think you will give me more time so I'm not going to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, witness, were you on the list that this man Omer had?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-075 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't even aware of a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have re-examination, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One clarifying question for Mr. Karadzic, we saw the list of -- I think it's the Prosecution exhibit, the list of 125 dead persons which we admitted as P3362. Do we see that word "sehid" on that list at all?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, that was Mr. Karadzic 's exhibit D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, D1115. Do we see the word on that document, Mr. Karadzic? Can you upload D1115?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to take a look now. The first page, the Army of BH, that's what it says there. The terminology is "sehid," unless it's a Christian, a Serb or a Croat. The BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where is it? You mean the title, Vojska BiH, you translate it as sehid? Where do we find the word "sehid"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Sehid" is the way it is usually put when speaking. "Sehid" is the word used for Muslims but not for Christians. Whoever gets killed in the army is called a sehid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you do concede that the word "sehid" does not appear on this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably not on this list. It says up here, Vojska BH, that is to say the Army of BH, the BH Army, and that has not been translated into English. Also, your Excellencies, this last rubric here, when it says, "Killed" that is killed in combat. And then if there is the word "preminvo," that means died a natural death. Whereas when it says "ubijen," that is killed as a result of a crime, a criminal act. So "poginvo" is killed in combat and "preminvo" is died a natural death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we are done with this document. Thank you for the clarification. Yes, Mr. Witness, that concludes your evidence. On behalf of this Chamber, as well as the Tribunal as a whole, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague yet again to give it. Now, you are free to go. Please have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait until we draw the curtain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we go into private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we need a short break in order to bring in the next witness? I doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, the Prosecution calls KDZ-052.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let the witness be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you kindly take the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please be seated and make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, I take it you have been told about this but you will be testifying today with the benefit of pseudonym, which is KDZ-052, and image distortion. This means that there will be no reference to your real name or information which might reveal your identity to the public or media. The audiovisual record of your testimony, which is broadcast to the public, will have a distorted image, like this. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's to ensure that your identity is protected and the transcript, while available to the public, will always refer to your pseudonym. So are you happy with this regime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 90277, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, you'll see a pseudonym sheet in front of you. Can this not be broadcast, please? It has your name and your date of birth. Can you, without saying either of your name or your date of birth, indicate whether that -- those details are correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3368 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, as we also discussed, part of your evidence in this case will be submitted in writing and we need to deal with a few formalities associated with that submission. You testified as a protected witness in the Brdjanin case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The pseudonym sheet is Exhibit P3363?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P3368, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You subsequently had an opportunity to review the audio recordings of that testimony?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You wish to correct two answers that you gave. The first one is on page -- transcript page 8061 at line 21. The answer Mico Djukic and his brother Milutin. Should properly read Rade Djukic and his brother Milutin, also known as Mico, unquote?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And at transcript page 8070, at line 1, the answer, "At the beginning, Serb soldiers. About 15 days later, the police came" should read, "At the beginning, Serb soldiers. About seven days later, the police came"? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you confirm that with these corrections the audio recording accurately reflects the evidence you gave at that time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions today, or if you were asked today about the same matters that you testified to in the Brdjanin case, would you provide the same information to the Trial Chamber, that is even if you wouldn't be able to formulate everything in the same words the essence of your answers would be the same?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 65 ter 00 -- 22087 under seal and 22087A which is a public redacted version of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Both admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 22087 will be Exhibit P3369 under seal and 65 ter 22087A will be Exhibit P3370.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: With Your Honour's leave, I'll read a summary of the witness's written evidence. Witness KDZ-052 was born and raised in the Sanski Most municipality. He testified about the check-point set up in 1992 in the area where he resided and the fact that only non-Serbs would be stopped and searched. He also testified that he heard on the radio at the end of May 1992 an announcement to the Muslims to surrender their weapons. The witness testified that the shelling and attack on Hrustovo and Vrhpolje was conducted by the 6th Krajina Brigade and it began at the end of May 1992. He gives evidence of the killings and the looting and burning of houses. The witness testified that troops surrounded the village of Kenjari on 27 June 1992. The villagers were rounded up and the men were separated from the women. A number of men were escorted to a house owned by a Croat, Marko Juric where they were visited by Vlado Vrkes. The following day the men were taken to Dujo Banovic's former house in the hamlet of Blazevici. The witness and a few of the younger men entered the house, the older men stayed in front of the house. The witness testified that a bomb was then thrown at the house. At this point, the witness and another man jumped out an open window at the back of a house -- at the back of the house. The other man ran away. The witness hid in a deep hole several metres from the house. The witness heard the men being thrown out of the house and a blast of fire directed toward the men which lasted about two minutes. The witness continued to hide in the hole. The killed men were brought into the house and the house was then set on fire. 18 persons died that day. The witness stayed in the deep hole until dawn the following day when he returned to his village. He observed all the houses had been burnt. The witness testified that he then went to Tomina where he joined other Muslims that had been displaced from Hrustovo and Vrhpolje. The Serbs drove this group of refugees to Krings facility in Sanski Most which is Schedule C, 22.4. The witness was detained in Krings for a month. Krings was first guarded by the military and after about seven days by the police. There were around 600 people detained there. The witness described the inhumane conditions at the camp including inadequate space and sanitary facilities, insufficient food, and no medical facilities. He gave evidence about beatings which began after the police came to guard the facility. Detainees were beaten with boots, batons and rifle butts. He testified that one detainee, Ejup Masic died as a result of the beating he received. The witness was released from Krings Hall in early August 1992 and left Sanski Most shortly thereafter on a convoy that went to Travnik. That completes the summary of the witness's written evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, I have very limited -- a very limited number of questions which I wish to ask you. First of all, I want to show you three photographs and the first one is 65 ter 05205. Sir, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes. That is the Krings hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Which of the buildings, the big red building, what building was that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes, we were detained in that big red building. There was nothing there except for a few old pieces of equipment and perhaps the remains of an old machine but that wasn't really much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the white building on the right-hand side of the photograph, do you know what that building is?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: We were brought into that building only once. I think there were offices there. Maybe the management offices of that company or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Why were you taken to that building?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: We were taken there to be interrogated by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3371, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter 05204, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you recognise what's depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: The Interior of the Krings hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3372, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I wasn't -- sorry, there is now a photo on the screen, which is 05207. I wasn't going to bother with this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, that was the building that you recognised in the earlier photograph of the Krings facility as the room or the building that you were taken to for interrogation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour, 05207.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit 3375.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 05209 on the screen, please. If we could go to page 7 of the English and page 7 of the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise these names that are listed here, 1 to 18?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Are these the names of -- well, you tell the Court who these people are?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: These people are the people who were killed and that I was there with, the village of Kenjar. They were killed. We were taken away and they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In the village of Blazevici?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was the age of the youngest person there on that day?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I think he was 14 or 15, Husein Kenjar, the son of Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, that's part of a larger report by the federal Ministry of the Interior affairs in Sarajevo regarding the exhumations in Hrustovo and Vrhpolje villages conducted in 1996. So I don't know -- I seek to only tender with this witness the page that I referred to which is page 7 in the English and B/C/S and we will seek to tender the entire document via the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted as Exhibit P3376.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Finally, I just have one question for you, sir. How many of your relatives or friends from Sanski Most municipality were killed in 1992? Or have been missing since 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to tell the Trial Chamber the number of people, either relatives of yours or friends, who were killed or have been missing since 1992?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I've lost three or four close relatives. As for friends and neighbours, there were too many of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will deal with the associated exhibits. I think we dealt with one already. We have three others. Did we deal with your leave to add an associated exhibit to the 65 ter list which was 65 ter 23455.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, and I seek leave to add that. That's mentioned in the witness's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we don't mind if they add it but we object to the admission of the exhibit because we don't think that it forms an indispensable part of the transcript because it's basically a report of an investigation and the witness, while having seen the report, just commented about names involved as opposed to any of the substance. We don't think that it should be sufficient to enable this to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You don't have any objection to the remaining two, 19921 and 19922?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The two will be admitted. And the simple way is for Ms. Sutherland to deal with this document with the witness right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could I have 65 ter 23 ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may say something before the break? There are over 70 pages of transcript, and in my experience so far, that would be testimony of a whole day. So I would appreciate it if you would reconsider one more time the time that you're willing to allot me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're asking for eight hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know what I was asking, but I'm asking for at least three or four hours because it is impossible to deal with this because this is the testimony of a whole day, and I am supposed to actually question the witness on this in a single hour or so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, but the witness started his evidence at around quarter to 4 one afternoon, on -- sorry I won't mention the day, and concluded his testimony at 6.22. So it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think he started in 2 past 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the transcript -- the transcript says recess taken at 3.40 p.m., on resuming, yes, you're right, Your Honour, 2 minutes past 4 and it finished at 6.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But there is another testimony. There is another testimony, and the transcript has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The Rule 92 ter package for this witness is the Brdjanin testimony only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the time, it's time to take a break. We will -- the tape is running out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll deal with this after the break and then I have one other question that I wanted to clarify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will resume at ten past 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness -- yes, let's finish your examination in chief, yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Sutherland. Sir, you will be further asked by the accused in his cross-examination. Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber considered the request. However, an hour for your cross-examination of this witness in the Chamber's view is more than sufficient. Just get on -- please get on with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. But for the transcript, I need to say -- in fact, are we in open session, right now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, I'd like to say that we've had a large number of witnesses that the Defence considers improperly questioned. That was the case with the previous witness as well. He was not questioned about many of the incidents, and it is quite impossible for us, Your Honour, because the statements created by the Prosecution are very complex and they speak of many incidents, not just one, because if it were for one incident alone, it would be much easier for us to cross-examine the witness. However, the witness repeats the whole story, and it is very difficult. And then, the Prosecutor gets up on his or her feet and says that the Defence did not really challenge that properly. Well, how can I challenge it when I'm not given the opportunity?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please don't waste your time. The Chamber's position has been made clear to you on several occasions. I won't repeat it. Please get on with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, were you familiar with the political developments in Bosnia and in your own municipality?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Well, I was never involved in politics. I was not really interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you familiar with negotiations on the future of Bosnia, and of your own municipality in the event that Bosnia became independent?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you are going to continue to complain about your shortage of time, I'll have to intervene with you. How are the negotiations relevant to this witness's evidence, which is talking about what he experienced as a victim mainly, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Excellency, that's not what we are talking about, he says that the Muslims were expelled from the police station. He was told this by his relative. What I'm trying to establish here is whether we should discuss matters and issues that he has no knowledge of and then just move on directly to the incident. And that's why I'm asking about his knowledge. Whether he knew that there were two police stations and that Muslims had not been expelled and that they could accept --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So did you know about this?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So why did you talk about these things in your statement? Your statement is replete with very generalised statements that you -- matters that you know nothing about.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, I was not involved in politics and I didn't really know what the situation was but I know that the policemen or actually it was being said that the policemen were expelled from the police station, then they moved to the municipal building and then a few days later they were expelled from there too and as far as I know they had been shot at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that is precisely the problem, witness. You're discussing matters that you have no knowledge of. Now, do you know that the Muslims could remain within the police station, the Serb police station, provided that they signed a statement?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can Mr. Karadzic keep his tone of voice down and let the witness answer, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And also provide references to me of the page number of the statements when he's going to put these assertions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, have you been following the question? Are you able to answer the question? Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't have enough time for all references and I should actually yell here at the Prosecutor, not the witness, because these statements are overly ambitious and I'm unable to test them in an hour's time. Now, witness shall -- if I ask the witness, is it correct that your relatives told you that these policemen were kicked out and -- but you didn't know that they could stay if they signed an oath of loyalty?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Well, that's correct, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I repeat: All witnesses are different, and some are indeed more difficult than others. Even every experienced lawyer conducting cross-examination has to deal with witnesses who may make broad and general statements or are difficult in some way or another. However, this does not mean that you should explore every single general statement a witness may make. As I emphasised several times earlier on, the point of cross-examination is to pick certain parts of evidence led in chief that can be challenged. Thus you should focus on challenging the evidence of the witness in certain areas, preferably where you have best material to do so. Please bear that in mind. And please stop making these statements about you being disadvantaged by difficult witnesses. Every lawyer has to deal with this problem. That's just the nature of trial in general. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps this was misinterpreted. I don't have the problem with this witness. I have a problem with insufficient time to test and challenge each of the positions forwarded by the Prosecutor in the statements. And whether these can be grounds for a conviction, because if they can or cannot, then I really cannot -- I'm not given an opportunity to challenge that. And my hands are tied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, his statements are not part of the evidence for this witness. It's his Brdjanin testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Sutherland. Please get on with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one final word. I am entitled to challenge the credibility of a witness and I cannot do that on the basis of one statement alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, witness, sir, you said that in 1991, check-points were set up. Is it correct, and did you actually go through these check-points, on numerous occasions and ask for your IDs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Well, I said the check-points were set up in 1992 and I did have occasion to go through them on a number of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. And of course they verified, they checked your papers, they checked your car, they didn't find anything suspicious and you were allowed through, correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You know, don't you, that Muslims and Croats did not join the JNA either as regular conscripts or as reserve staff but Serbs did, correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You know -- also know that Serbs who had up until recently, as you stated, been civilians, once the mobilisation was in place, they joined the 6th Krajina Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You have also stated that up until 27 June, in 1992, there were no disturbances of any kind in your village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Well, I think about three kilometres, maybe four.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that Hrustovo and Vrhpolje had 300 Muslims, there was an armed formation in Hrustovo of 300 armed Muslims, whereas there were a total of some 900 fighters in that area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I think that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that fighting began in Prijedor, which is some 20 kilometres away from Sanski Most, and that this fighting broke out on 23 May?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the entire valley of the Sana river, Kljuc, Sanski Most, Prijedor, Bosanski Novi, all those places, in all those places there was a series of attacks by the Patriotic League and the Green Berets against Serb -- the Serbian army and Serb villages between the 25th and 27th?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Well, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that that is how the fighting began in late May, in other words between 23 May and 31 May, there was major fighting between the Muslim army and -- the Muslim soldiers and the Serbian army there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Well, I was unable to leave my village, and in late May I wasn't even unable to go to Sanski Most. In other words, the tensions were already too high. So I couldn't know anything about the developments in Prijedor, Bosanski Novi or Kljuc or anywhere like that. I didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you said that you were in Hrustovo in late May?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a lot of fighting in late May in Hrustovo?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Well, at the time when I was in Hrustovo the fighting had just begun.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What fighting was this, between whom?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Well, this was fighting between Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which units were present there from -- on the Serb side and which Muslim units were there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I don't know about the Serb units, but in Hrustovo village, there were a few men who remained there, but as for units, an organised armed force there, I know nothing about that. I didn't see anyone there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how long did the fighting last in Hrustovo?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: When the fighting started, I stayed in Hrustovo perhaps two more days. On the second day after the fighting started I left Hrustovo and moved to the neighbouring (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you spent a few days with this relative. I don't want to mention his name. Why didn't you go to your own home instead?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Because he asked me to bring his mother, who was also in Hrustovo at the time, visiting her daughter, and he said his place might be safer than Hrustovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why would his home be safer than yours?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Because he had Serb neighbours, and he must have discussed it with them, and it was decided that it was safer. There was no fighting there, whereas there was fighting in Hrustovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So for a whole month after the fighting in Hrustovo, nobody

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: That's correct, not until 27 June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I seek a redaction on page 48, lines 13 and 25, and I'm wondering about page 50, line 17. The village that was mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And also, sorry, line 51 -- page 51, line 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then in the future, I'll refer to it as your village. Are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You've said that before the conflict and at the outbreak of the conflict, you saw different units around town wearing a variety of uniforms. How would you describe it briefly? What kind of units were they? What kind of uniforms, what kind of insignia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: You mean in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: In Sanski Most, I was able to see a lot of soldiers, reservists, military policemen, civilian police, and the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As far as the army is concerned, they all wore the same uniforms and the police wore the same uniforms, but you said you saw a variety of uniforms. Did you see any more uniforms with different insignia? You said that in the trial from which we have your transcript that was admitted.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I saw camouflage uniforms and the regular green olive-grey uniforms, and the insignia were the Serbian Tricolour, and I'm not sure about that sign with the coat of arms with the four S. I think I saw that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your evidence on page ending with 081, you said you had not seen any insignia at all.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was page 8081 in that testimony you gave. Is it true that you said, and you were aware, that on 28 May the Serbs announced on the radio that all Muslims had to turn over their weapons, those who turned over their weapons will be allowed to go to Tominska Palanka, a Muslim hamlet near Tomina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true, witness, that Serb soldiers took civilians from Hrustovo and Vrhpolje to Tominska Palanka while the fighting lasted?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: That time I was not in Hrustovo so I cannot confirm but I heard later from other people that they had been taken to Tominska Palanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But towards the end of May, you were in Hrustovo, why?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were not living in your village, were you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I don't think you understood. I lived in my village first. Then I moved to the other village where my relative lived, which is the native village of my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you openly, witness: After the fighting in Hrustovo, did you actually find shelter with your relative rather than your own home?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: It was into the second day of the fighting that he invited me to move to his place. But the fighting continued after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: P761, a document under 92 bis, is a statement I would recommend to everyone's attention. The witness described how a Serbian unit looked after a group of civilians one whole day before moving them to Tomina. Is that also in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a comment by Mr. Karadzic, he should be putting questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All the question he put so far in relation to that statement is that -- is just a confirmation of the place, Tomina. I look forward to hearing any questions. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tomina is also in your municipality and it's a mixed Serb-Muslim village; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Tomina is a village in Sanski Most municipality but it was not really mixed. It was rather separated. Tominska Palanka for instance was an exclusively Muslim place. The other part was almost purely Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're talking about two hamlets in the same village.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when you came there, you moved into Muslim houses, the mosque was still standing, and there was no fighting in Tomina, correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: The mosque was still standing, I think, there was no fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you were taken away to Krings, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, witness, I would like to know about 4 August, when you were released. How could the authorities afford to release such a dangerous witness of such a dangerous incident? Did the authorities know about the incident and that you were involved in it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I think the policemen who interrogated me were not aware of that incident. And if I had told them I had survived it, I am certain I wouldn't be sitting here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So they didn't know about it. Did any other authorities know?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I don't know. You have to ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you stayed in Sanski Most for a while. Was it difficult to get on the list for transport?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: You mean to leave Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: There was no list, I think. They just said on the radio that whoever wants to leave Sanski Most should go to the main road, that buses would be provided, and we would somehow be shipped out of there. You didn't have to register anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they ask you for any money for the ticket?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have to produce some certificates that you had paid your taxes or something like that? Was there any paperwork?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: From Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: To Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you joined the army, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: No. Certainly not. I took the first chance I got to leave Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then when did you give the first statement about this incident?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: After Sanski Most was liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how come you failed to give a statement about such a drastic incident as soon as you came to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I wouldn't have known who to approach in Travnik. Chaos reigned there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will go back to the incident in a moment. But before that, what about the people from your village and the other village where you stayed or the hamlet that bears the same name an as your relatives? Did they look for any weapons there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: They said everybody should surrender weapons and those people who had licensed weapons, hunting weapons and pistols, surrendered them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there any automatic rifles there and weapons in illegal possession?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you turn over any weapons that a friend of yours took to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did you turn over?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: An automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. There was a debate among you whether to hand in the weapons or not, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when did you hand your weapon in, around what date?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date. Perhaps two days after the shooting started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then if that was on 28 May, for the next 27 days you did not have any more problems; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then Mr. Karanovic came, you say, with some reservists to that hamlet and started searching houses; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And those searches for weapons lasted until 27 June?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Which day you said they started? They actually started one morning with the searches, they took two hours, and then they took us away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They told you to gather at an intersection, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You described them as local reservists. What kind of insignia did you see on them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Can't remember any more. But they were all locals. People who lived nearby. Some of them wore uniforms, some of them wore parts of uniforms. One would have the shirt of a uniform. Another would have the trousers of the uniform. Some had weapons, some had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What would you say what unit was it or were they perhaps not even a unit and under whose command were they?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you were taken from that intersection, you were taken to the Blazevic house?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: They told us we were being taken to be interrogated because they suspected some of us still had weapons. And when we came to the school, they went on, they didn't even stop, and then we came to Marko Juric's house. We spent one whole day there. This one man left us saying he was going to look for the command because there was nobody around that house. That was in the morning. We spent the whole day there. And he did not reappear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's this Karanovic person; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say on 28 June Vlado Vrkes stopped by, he was surprised and asked you what you were doing there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes, a man came that day. We didn't know him. Then he introduced himself as Vlado Vrkes, president of the SDS in Sanski Most. And he asked us, what are you doing there? And we explained that we had been taken away from our homes to be interrogated. He told us not to worry, that we would probably be exchanged for Serbs elsewhere in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you did not recognise him?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: I couldn't recognise him because I didn't know him. I knew nothing about politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm confused because in that statement given in 1996, that 65 ter 22086, page 2, you said you recognised him as soon as he appeared.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: It must be some sort of mistake. I didn't know him. He introduced himself by name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And he said you shouldn't worry, nothing to worry about, you will probably be part of an exchange?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then he left, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
utterances.text: Yes, he left. He was with us for a very short while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then Karanovic returned that afternoon and escorted you to where?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-052
